output.brief:
Priya — don't roll back 6.14; it isn't the cause.

At 10:38 UTC on 3 March, Corvane, our edge-protection vendor, auto-installed a new rule pack. One new rule, AUTO-LIB-17, blocks password logins from the 'nettle-http' library that every Android app version uses. Since 10:41 it has blocked ~9,700 requests a day from 41,300 app installs, 92% with recent successful logins: customers, not bots. iOS, web and quick-unlock don't match the rule, so only Android password logins collapsed (96% to 8%).

6.14 is ruled out: the drop is identical on versions 6.11–6.13 and on every Android OS release, with or without the March security patch, and began on all versions within a minute. The later 14:00 token change is not involved.

Next: have Corvane set the rules added on 3 March to log-only on the password-login path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules on, then confirm Android password success recovers to ~96%. Don't raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the reported rate; that worsens or hides the problem. Then require testing before vendor rule updates.

Confidence: about 90%. Unproven: how much of the 18% call rise this explains versus the fee mailing.
